original_question: For an even integer m, which non-bipartite triangle-free graph with m edges has the largest spectral radius? Equivalently, among all non-bipartite graphs G with m edges and no C_3 subgraph, determine the extremal graph maximizing lambda(G).
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the C3-free subsection’s even-size non-bipartite extremal problem: determine, for even m, the graph of maximum adjacency spectral radius among all non-bipartite triangle-free graphs with m edges. This is the problem formally posed after the odd-m Zhai–Shu extremal result and before the theorem identifying the three even-m extremal families.
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the core extremal problem right: it fixes the number of edges m, imposes the triangle-free (i.e. C3-free) condition, excludes bipartite graphs, and asks for the graph maximizing the spectral radius λ(G). That is exactly the mathematical content of the even-size non-bipartite triangle-free spectral extremal problem discussed in the paper’s C3-free line of results.
missing_details: The paper works with simple, undirected graphs.
In the edge-spectral Turán setting, isolated vertices are ignored when the number of edges is fixed; this convention should be made explicit if the question is to be fully stand-alone.
λ(G) should be identified as the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix A(G).
The quantifier should say that m is a positive even integer.
If one wants the formulation to track the surrounding paper-faithful context, the question arises because the odd-m extremal construction from the previous theorem is only defined when m is odd.

If one wants to align with the nearby solved theorem rather than just the motivating question, one must specify the large-m hypothesis used in that theorem and the dependence of the extremal graph on m mod 3.
The draft does not indicate whether it is asking for a conjectural/open formulation or for the already-proved determination of the extremal graph.
The draft does not state uniqueness of the extremal graph, which is part of the nearby theorem-level formulation.
refined_question: Let λ(G) denote the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of a simple undirected graph G, and, as usual in the fixed-size edge-spectral Turán problem, ignore isolated vertices. For a positive even integer m, determine the extremal graph among all non-bipartite triangle-free graphs G with |E(G)|=m that maximizes λ(G).
justification: The draft is closest to the paper’s even-m non-bipartite triangle-free extremal problem itself, not to a broader forbidden-odd-cycle variant. In the surrounding context, the paper first recalls the sharp odd-m bound via the subdivided K_{2,(m-1)/2} construction, then explains that this extremal graph exists only for odd m, and explicitly asks for the even-m analogue. Immediately after that, it defines the candidate extremal graphs for the even case and states the theorem determining them. So the faithful stand-alone refinement should keep the scope exactly at non-bipartite triangle-free graphs of fixed even size, while making explicit the graph model, the meaning of λ(G), and the convention about isolated vertices.
